summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore, driven by tractors (+36.29%) while cranes were flat at ₹52.86 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14.98% YoY to ₹104.93 crore and EBITDA rose 10.84% to ₹13.09 crore. Tractor revenue grew 36.29% to ₹52.08 crore, while crane revenue was flat at ₹52.86 crore, which management attributed to the Tier III to Tier V emission norm transition and full utilisation of the existing crane plant. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 20–25% overall revenue growth and 12.5–13% standalone EBITDA margin. The new Bhud plant is targeted for commercial production by end-November 2026, with tower crane production planned for the new line.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.08 crore, up 36.29% YoY. Management guides 25–30% FY27 growth; utilisation of ~12,000-unit capacity is about 35–40%, and no capacity addition planned. Dealer network about 225.

segments.name: Cranes
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ₹52.86 crore, flat YoY. Existing plant at full capacity (~1,000–1,200 units); guidance 15–20% FY27 growth from existing plant. Dealer network about 25, stagnant for three quarters. New Bhud plant capacity 3,600 units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth maintained at ~20–25% (existing plant only; new plant contribution mainly assumed in Q4).
Tractor revenue growth ~25–30% in FY27; management says 30%-plus over 3–5 years.
Crane revenue growth ~15–20% in FY27 from existing plant.
Standalone EBITDA margin 12.5–13% for FY27; consolidated margin said to be similar to last year (~14–15% per analyst’s reading).

New Bhud plant: commercial production targeted by end-November 2026; machinery expected in October. First year utilisation ~30% (Q1 of operations), 35–40% next quarter, ~40–45% average in FY28 (1,500–1,800 cranes).
Crane price hike taken; further price hike planned in coming months; management expects cost pass-through from Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: New Bhud crane plant: 3,600-unit capacity; civil work in progress; almost all major machines ready; commercial production targeted by end-November 2026.
Tower crane: first prototype passed testing; first lot of 10 machines targeted within Q2 FY27, subject to imported components; some tower crane numbers to be built at the old factory.
Capex funds: ~₹45 crore still held in bank; management says it will be fully deployed by March, possibly by buying 6–8 of 10 planned machines and deferring the rest by up to three months.
Tractor capacity ~12,000 units; no addition planned. Crane machine shop utilisation ~80–85%; crane assembly ~30–35%.
demand_pricing: Crane dealers ~25 (stagnant for three quarters vs. 50-plus target cited by analyst); management plans ~20–25 more dealers within six to12 months of new plant start; Shubham cited a roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years.
Some existing dealers being replaced to match performance expectations; management says working in only ~20–25% of the addressable area.
Tractor dealers ~225; growth tied to dealer development, retail financing, and village-level demos.
Barota Finance finances ~20% of new Indo Farm tractors; refinances old tractors of all brands.
Crane competitors cited: Escorts Construction (premium pricing) and one Faridabad-based peer at similar pricing. Peer ACE grew more than 20% per analyst.
Management says tractor price hikes will follow industry; crane price hike already taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crane input cost increase been passed on, and will margins normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold from Q2 as demand improves; the Tier III to V transition took about three quarters to stabilise, and cost increases can now be passed on.

qa_highlights.question: Why is crane dealer count stagnant at 25, and what is the plan to absorb new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Dealers to be added once capacity is in place; some dealers replaced. Roadmap of ~60-plus dealers nationally, taking one to one-and-a-half years. FY28 needs ~20–25 dealers to sell 1,500–1,800 cranes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the crane sales volume and YoY volume growth in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not provided on the call; management said figures would be shared by email via the Finance Head.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tractor utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor utilisation ~35–40%; assembly ~30–35%; machine shop ~80–85% because many crane components are made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA margin on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone guidance 12.5–13%; consolidated said to move on similar lines to last year, which the analyst interpreted as 14–15%; management confirmed the analyst’s reading.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹45 crore capex cash be used by Q3 to start commercialisation by January?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may buy 6–8 of 10 machines and defer up to three months; full deployment by March. Commercial production still targeted for November.

qa_highlights.question: Can crane growth of 15–20% be achieved with existing capacity before the new plant starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed existing capacity is sufficient for 15–20% growth until the new plant starts.

risks_watch: Crane growth: Q1 flat; FY27 guidance 15–20% depends on July–August demand recovery and dealer additions.
Bhud plant timing: November commercial production depends on machinery arriving in October and on imported tower crane components.
Dealer quality and ramp-up: management says new dealers take 6–18 months; utilisation of new plant guided at 30% in year one.
Tractor volume growth of 25–30% contingent on dealer build-out, financing, and village-level demand; utilisation still ~35–40%.
Price hikes: crane price increase taken; further hikes depend on demand and input costs; tractor pricing follows industry.
Volume disclosure: Q1 unit volumes not disclosed on the call; to be shared later by email.
summary.management_tone: Confident on tractors and the new plant timeline, but evasive on specifics: crane dealer targets, unit volumes, and consolidated margin were deferred or loosely answered. Management repeatedly tied crane recovery to Q2 demand without quantifying it.
key_quotes: From this quarter onwards, because demand has increased, I think everything can be passed on to the customers.
We expect to complete these 10 machines within this quarter, subject to receipt of the few components we are expecting from outside.
The new capacity is 3,600 cranes, yes.
Over three to five years in the tractor business, we are very sure that 30% -plus growth will continue.
